Exact conditional Poisson regression

Source: R/special-models.R
exact_poisson.Rd

Conditional inference for one coefficient of a Poisson log linear model (Cox 1970; Hirji 2006), as in Stata's expoisson discussed by Hilbe (2014, sec. 9.4). The counts are conditioned on their totals within the strata, which removes the intercept and the stratum effects; the conditional distribution of T = sum(x * y) is computed exactly by polynomial convolution. Returns the conditional maximum likelihood estimate (which equals the unconditional Poisson estimate with stratum intercepts when it is finite), the median unbiased estimate when T is at an end of its support, the exact two sided p value of beta = 0 (probability method), and the exact confidence interval.

Usage

exact_poisson(y, x, strata = NULL, exposure = NULL, level = 0.95)

Arguments

y

Counts.

x

Integer covariate whose coefficient is tested.

strata

Optional factor of strata (nuisance effects).

exposure

Optional exposure (offset on the rate scale).

level

Confidence level.

Value

A list with estimate, type ("CMLE" or "MUE"), p_value, conf_int, statistic (observed T) and the conditional distribution support and counts (log weights).

Examples

exact_poisson(y = c(0, 1, 3, 4), x = c(0, 0, 1, 1), exposure = c(10, 12, 9, 11))
#> $estimate
#> [1] 2.04122
#> 
#> $type
#> [1] "CMLE"
#> 
#> $p_value
#> [1] 0.0315777
#> 
#> $conf_int
#> [1] -0.01082803  5.84941620
#> 
#> $level
#> [1] 0.95
#> 
#> $statistic
#> [1] 7
#> 
#> $support
#> [1] 0 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8
#> 
#> $log_weights
#> [1] -5.173017 -3.188886 -2.031433 -1.433596 -1.305763 -1.624217 -2.412674
#> [8] -3.760747 -5.935499
#>
